fields.title: Settings shows the Internal Work Orders toggle, off, with its description
fields.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Use a new organization in which the Internal Work Orders setting has never been switched on.
fields.custom_steps: 1. Open Settings > Work Orders.
fields.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • A toggle "Internal Work Orders" shows on the tab, written in Title Case like the other toggles.
  • The toggle is off.
  • Its description reads "Lets you flag your own company as an internal customer and mark a customer's work order, or a single line of a billable work order, as No Charge (warranty, goodwill, comeback). Internal and no-charge work orders close without an invoice; their parts cost posts to the expense account of their category instead of Cost of Parts."

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.0 final (9 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11758 (Story 1, Turn on Internal Work Orders, flag internal customers, manage categories), story SV-11766 (Story 9, Reports, dashboard and exports)

  • S1-R1: “Settings > Work Orders shows a toggle "Internal Work Orders" (Title Case like the other toggles on the tab), off by default, organization-wide like the other toggles, with the description "Lets you flag your own company as an internal customer and mark a customer's work order, or a single line of a billable work order, as No Charge (warranty, goodwill, comeback). Internal and no-charge work orders close without an invoice; their parts cost posts to the expense account of their category instead of Cost of Parts."”
  • Feature Overview: “Two kinds of work order, one way to close them.”
  • Terminology: “Internal Work Orders → the name of the setting under Settings > Work Orders and of the report under Reports; both cover internal and no-charge work orders, as does the Technician Efficiency chip "Internal work orders: Hide / Only internal / Show all" (tooltip "Internal and no-charge work orders", S9-R3). On a flagged customer's work order the badge reads Internal, never No Charge.”

S1-02.section_name: Turn on Internal Work Orders, internal customers and categories
S1-02.title: First turn-on opens the customer picker window with Save disabled
S1-02.automation: AUTOMATION: Not available on Build to test Yet - Last checked 11/12/2026

fields.title: First turn-on opens the customer picker window with Save disabled
fields.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Use a new organization in which the Internal Work Orders setting has never been switched on.
fields.custom_steps:
1. Open Settings > Work Orders.
  2. Switch the "Internal Work Orders" toggle on.
fields.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The toggle "Internal Work Orders" is off.

Step 2:

  • A window titled "Which customers are your own company?" opens.
  • It has a customer picker with search, and no customer is picked.
  • Under the picker the hint reads "Pick up to 50 customers here. Flag more from Edit Customer."
  • The line "You can change this any time: Customers > Edit Customer > Internal customer." shows.
  • It has the buttons "Do this later" and "Save"; "Save" is disabled.
  • The window lists no customer as already flagged.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.0 final (9 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11758 (Story 1, Turn on Internal Work Orders, flag internal customers, manage categories)

  • S1-R2: “Switching the toggle from off to on for the first time in the organization opens the modal "Which customers are your own company?" with the body "Work orders for these customers are internal: no prices and no invoice; parts cost posts to the expense account of their category when you use QuickBooks or AccountingHub. Nothing is picked for you: your location is not always a customer, and the names can differ. Pick one or more, or do it later from the customer page.", a customer picker (the standard customer Select with search, several customers can be picked, each shown as a chip with a remove control; up to 50, with the hint "Pick up to 50 customers here. Flag more from Edit Customer."), the line "You can change this any time: Customers > Edit Customer > Internal customer." and the buttons "Do this later" and "Save". No customer is preselected. Save is disabled until at least one customer is picked. Save saves the toggle (on) and flags the picked customers in one step (only this toggle and the flags; other unsaved changes on the tab wait for Save settings; to back out, the user switches the toggle off and saves settings), closes the modal and then shows the dialog of S1-R11 for each picked customer with open billable work orders, one after another; the page shows the toggle on and the hint lines of S1-R3 with nothing left to save for this setting. Closing the modal with X acts as "Do this later" (S1-R5); Esc and a click outside do nothing, as in every dialog of the app. The modal is shown once per organization: switching the toggle on again later opens nothing (S1-R10). Switching it off opens nothing. The modal never lists who is flagged, and Settings > Work Orders never lists customers.”
  • User Feedback Summary: “First-time modal, more than 50 customers | "Pick up to 50 customers here. Flag more from Edit Customer." | Hint under the customer picker (S1-R2)”
  • Story 1, Entry points: “Not on New Customer, not in a Settings list and not on the work order itself: a work order becomes internal only through its customer. Removing the flag: unticking the checkbox (S1-R6), allowed any time with the info dialog of S1-R12. Who is flagged is visible on the Customers list and the customer header (S1-R8), not in Settings.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.

fields.title: Picking two customers and Save turns the setting on and flags both
fields.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Use a new organization in which the Internal Work Orders setting has never been switched on.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer A with no open work orders.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer B with no open work orders.
fields.custom_steps:
1. Open Settings > Work Orders.
  2. Switch the "Internal Work Orders" toggle on.
  3. Type customer A's name in the customer picker.
  4. Pick customer A.
  5. Type customer B's name in the customer picker.
  6. Pick customer B.
  7. Click Save.
  8. Open the Customers list.

Expected Result

  • The toggle is off.

Step 2:

  • The "Which customers are your own company?" window opens.

  • Customer A is offered.

  • Customer A shows as a chip with a remove control.
  • "Save" becomes enabled.

Step 5:

  • Customer B is offered.

  • Customer B shows as a second chip with a remove control.

Step 7:

  • The window closes.
  • The toggle shows on.
  • The hint lines show under the description.
  • Nothing is left to save for this setting: leaving the page asks nothing about unsaved changes for it.

Step 8:

  • Customer A and customer B each show an "Internal" badge next to their name.

It is shown while the setting is on (S1-N4 for the exception). New Customer does not show it: a customer is flagged after it exists, from Edit Customer or the modal. The checkbox and the modal are the only places the flag is set; ticking it on Save flags the customer (with the dialog of S1-R11 when open billable work orders exist).”
  • S1-R8: “While the setting is on, a flagged customer shows an "Internal" badge next to its name in the customer header, in the customers list and on the customers list mobile card. While the setting is off the badge is hidden in all three places (S1-N4); the badges on work orders stay (S2-R10).”
  • S1-R11: “When a customer is flagged (Save in the modal, or on Edit Customer with the checkbox ticked), or the setting is turned on again while flagged customers have open billable work orders (S1-R10), a dialog reads "[n] open work orders for [customer] are billable. Make them internal? Prices, fees and discounts are removed; costs and hours are kept." and lists those work orders under the body, one line each (number, location, unit, status), at every location the user has access to, up to 10 rows and then "and [n] more". Counted as open: every billable work order of that customer that is not invoiced, not paid and not Declined, Estimates included. A row with a deposit carries the note "Deposit: stays billable"; a row with a posted vendor bill carries the note "Vendor bill: cost moves at Close" (no dialog of S2-R8 per work order on this path). Buttons: "Keep billable" and "Make internal". Make internal applies S2-R7 to every listed work order without a deposit; those with a deposit stay billable until the deposit is reversed and the dialog is shown again. Keep billable leaves them as they are; they finish with an invoice as today. Open no-charge work orders of that customer are not listed: they stay no charge with their category and keep Change category and Convert to Billable (S2-R6). With no open billable work orders the dialog is not shown. Saving Edit Customer for a customer that carries the flag shows this dialog again whenever that customer has open billable work orders, so work orders left billable earlier (a deposit since reversed, Keep billable, a user without 'Work Orders — Create & Edit') can be made internal later. Open billable work orders at locations the user has no access to are not listed; the line "[n] more at locations you don't have access to." under the list says how many, and they are converted when a user with access saves Edit Customer or the setting is turned on again (S1-R10). Make internal converts the listed work orders without switching location. A pending portal estimate of a work order made internal is no longer available: the portal refuses approval with "This estimate is no longer available." and shows the existing obsolete banner, since internal work orders are never on the portal (S2-R11).”
  • Key Decisions, Permissions (Action | Needs | Without it): “See the Internal badge on the customers list and the customer header | Customers page access | Not applicable”
  • Terminology: “Internal customer → one of the shop's existing customers flagged as the shop's own company or a sister company. Set in the modal that opens the first time the setting is switched on, or at the bottom of Edit Customer; nowhere else. Several allowed. Not a system customer: ShopView creates nothing.”
  • Feature Overview: “Internal work orders come from internal customers. The shop flags its own company (and any sister company) as an internal customer once: in the modal that opens the first time the Internal Work Orders setting is switched on (nobody is preselected: the location is not necessarily a customer and the names differ), or later with the Internal customer checkbox at the bottom of Edit Customer. Settings > Work Orders holds the toggle, that one-time modal and two hints: a link to the categories page and a link to the QuickBooks mapping. Every internal customer carries a default internal category, General Internal unless changed on Edit Customer; an asset of an internal customer can carry its own category (Edit Asset).   • S1-R11: “When a customer is flagged (Save in the modal, or on Edit Customer with the checkbox ticked), or the setting is turned on again while flagged customers have open billable work orders (S1-R10), a dialog reads "[n] open work orders for [customer] are billable. Make them internal? Prices, fees and discounts are removed; costs and hours are kept." and lists those work orders under the body, one line each (number, location, unit, status), at every location the user has access to, up to 10 rows and then "and [n] more". Counted as open: every billable work order of that customer that is not invoiced, not paid and not Declined, Estimates included. A row with a deposit carries the note "Deposit: stays billable"; a row with a posted vendor bill carries the note "Vendor bill: cost moves at Close" (no dialog of S2-R8 per work order on this path). Buttons: "Keep billable" and "Make internal". Make internal applies S2-R7 to every listed work order without a deposit; those with a deposit stay billable until the deposit is reversed and the dialog is shown again. Keep billable leaves them as they are; they finish with an invoice as today. Open no-charge work orders of that customer are not listed: they stay no charge with their category and keep Change category and Convert to Billable (S2-R6). With no open billable work orders the dialog is not shown. Saving Edit Customer for a customer that carries the flag shows this dialog again whenever that customer has open billable work orders, so work orders left billable earlier (a deposit since reversed, Keep billable, a user without 'Work Orders — Create & Edit') can be made internal later. Open billable work orders at locations the user has no access to are not listed; the line "[n] more at locations you don't have access to." under the list says how many, and they are converted when a user with access saves Edit Customer or the setting is turned on again (S1-R10). Make internal converts the listed work orders without switching location. A pending portal estimate of a work order made internal is no longer available: the portal refuses approval with "This estimate is no longer available." and shows the existing obsolete banner, since internal work orders are never on the portal (S2-R11).”
  • S2-R7: “Changing the customer on a work order works as today (not offered on an invoiced or paid billable work order, as today, nor on a closed internal or no-charge work order, S2-R9); until then the classification follows the new customer: to an internal customer the work order becomes internal (prices removed, costs and hours kept, no Convert actions); to a regular customer from an internal one it becomes billable (lines priced as in S2-R6). A No Charge mark and its category survive a change to another regular customer; a no-charge work order moved to an internal customer becomes internal and loses its category. The Change Customer dialog says what will happen to the prices and, when the work order stays internal or no charge, adds "Shop supplies resets to [customer]'s minimum ($[amount])." (without 'See Financial Data' the sentence omits the amount).”
  • Key Decisions: “Flagging a customer offers to make its open billable work orders internal; removing the flag is free and leaves open internal work orders internal.”
  • S2-R13: “The classification is written on the work order when it is created, when its customer changes and when it is converted; the closed record carries it too, with the category. Lists, reports and integrations read it from there, never from the customer flag. Converting to no charge or to billable, changing the category, a shop supplies amount change, Make internal (S1-R11, on each work order), Close with its posting date, Reopen, and adding or removing a customer's Internal flag are recorded in the work order or customer Audit Log with the user and the time.”

fields.custom_steps: 1. Open Administration > Service > Internal Work Orders.
fields.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The page has two tabs, Internal categories and No Charge categories.
  • The Internal categories tab shows the columns Category, QuickBooks expense account (with the green QuickBooks mark), Internal customers using it, and Work orders.
  • General Internal is listed with a "Default" badge.
  • Each row has a menu with Edit and Archive.
  • The buttons "New Internal Category" and "New No Charge Category" show.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.0 final (9 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11758 (Story 1, Turn on Internal Work Orders, flag internal customers, manage categories), story SV-11759 (Story 2, An internal or no-charge work order from creation to Close)

  • S1-R13: “Administration > Service > Internal Work Orders is a page with two tabs. Internal categories: columns Category (the default carries a Default badge), QuickBooks expense account (with the QuickBooks mark; "Not set" with a warning icon when empty), Internal customers using it, Work orders (count, all time; a billable work order with a no-charge line of the category counts too), and a row menu with Edit and Archive. No Charge categories: Category, QuickBooks expense account, Original work order (Required / Not asked), Work orders, row menu. Buttons "New Internal Category" and "New No Charge Category". The starting set is seeded for every organization when this release ships, so the categories, the QuickBooks rows (S5-R5) and the hub rows (S6-R2) exist before the setting is turned on; turning the setting on seeds nothing: General Internal (default, cannot be archived); Warranty (requires the original work order), Goodwill (does not), Comeback (requires). Archived categories stay on the work orders and lines that used them and in the report filter under Archived; a "Show archived (n)" link lists them with Restore. The page needs 'Settings — Service', like every Administration > Service page; while the setting is off it shows the notice "Internal Work Orders is off. Turn it on in Settings > Work Orders." and the lists stay editable. Each list holds up to 100 active categories; past that, the New button is disabled with "You can have up to 100 active categories in this list. Archive one to add another." The QuickBooks expense account column is shown only while the current location is connected to QuickBooks.”
  • S1-R16: “A category has a stable key; renaming it keeps the history, the report filter and the mappings. Archiving a category in use keeps it on existing work orders, lines, documents and reports; it is no longer offered in any select. The default Internal category cannot be archived; changing the default moves nothing on existing customers. The green QuickBooks mark (the existing QuickBooks icon) is shown wherever a field maps to QuickBooks: the account columns and pickers of S1-R13 and S1-R14, the asset field of S1-R15 and the Settings hint of S1-R3. Archiving a category that is the stored default of customers or assets first shows "[n] internal customers and [m] assets use this category as their default. Their new work orders will use the next category in line." The stored value stays on the customer and the asset, shown as "[name] (archived)" with the hint "Archived. Pick an active category."; resolution for a new work order (S2-R1) skips archived categories: the asset's, else the customer's, else the default Internal category, the first active one wins. Restore puts everything back as it was.”
  • Terminology: “Category → a shop-managed entry in one of two lists on Administration > Service > Internal Work Orders: Internal categories (where the cost of work on the shop's own equipment goes) and No Charge categories (why a customer's work order or line is free). Each carries a QuickBooks expense account per location and, on No Charge, whether it requires the original work order. Replaces "reason".”
  • Key Decisions: “Categories are shop-managed and carry the account; the work order never asks an accounting question. The category of an internal work order is resolved from the asset, else the customer, else General Internal; a no-charge category is picked where No Charge is set.”

  • S2-R1: “In the New Work Order dialog, picking a customer with the Internal customer flag shows the "Internal" badge next to the customer name with an info icon; the tooltip reads "Internal customer: no prices, no invoice. There is no checkbox to tick and no category to pick on the work order. The work order is created internal with the category resolved as: the asset's Internal category (S1-R15), else the customer's default (S1-R7), else the default Internal category; it is re-resolved while the work order is open when the asset changes or when the category of the asset or the customer is edited (a closed work order never changes), archived categories are skipped (S1-R16), and it can be changed on the asset or the customer, never on the work order.   • S2-N3: “If the selected customer is an internal customer, the "No Charge" checkbox is not shown in the New Work Order dialog and a billable work order of that customer offers no Convert action (S2-R2, S2-R7). Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.0 final (9 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11759 (Story 2, An internal or no-charge work order from creation to Close)

  • S2-R2: “In the New Work Order dialog (New Work Order only; Edit Work Order, which shares the dialog, is unchanged), picking a customer without the flag shows, at the bottom of the dialog below the "Asset Here?" checkbox and separated from it by a divider, an unticked checkbox "No Charge" with an info icon whose tooltip reads "Warranty, goodwill or comeback work. Closes without an invoice; parts cost posts to the expense account of the category." Ticking it reveals the required select "Category" listing the active No Charge categories, empty by default; Save is refused with the field message "Pick a category" until one is picked. When the category requires the original work order, the select "Original work order" appears under it (the customer's invoiced and closed work orders at the locations the user has access to, those on the same asset first, each as number, date and first line, and "Not in ShopView" under Other), optional here, with the helper "Which earlier work order this job comes from, or Not in ShopView, and the line on it. The line sets the original technician for the comeback and warranty numbers. Optional here, required at Close."; once a work order is picked, the optional select "Original line" lists its lines (number, title, technician). The checkbox is hidden when the selected customer is an internal customer and for users without 'See Financial Data'. Ticked, the work order is created No Charge with that category. It works whether or not any customer is flagged. As soon as a work order or a line is picked, the line "Original technician: [names]" (or "Original technician: none") shows under the selects, so a wrong attribution is seen and corrected by picking the line before anything is saved.”
  • S2-R17: “When the category requires the original work order, every dialog that sets the category (New Work Order S2-R2, Convert to No Charge S2-R5, Change category S2-R6, and the line dialogs of Story 12) shows the selects "Original work order" and "Original line" of S2-R2. Both are optional in the dialogs; the original work order is required at Close (S3-R2) and before Create invoice on a no-charge line (S12-R9); "Not in ShopView" satisfies it. The original technicians are derived when saved and stored with the work order or the line: every technician the original line shows, however they were assigned, by hand or from a schedule shift (a line with several technicians gives several, and the comeback counts once for each in the report); without an original line, the technician assigned to the original work order; without one, or with "Not in ShopView", none, and the report shows the job under Unassigned so it stays in the totals. They are shown in the dialog as soon as the original is picked, in the report (S9-R2) and in the hub record (S8-R1). The original work order is a link on the document, in the notes and in the report.”

  • The header card has an orange outline and a light orange background.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.0 final (9 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11759 (Story 2, An internal or no-charge work order from creation to Close)

  • S2-R3: “The work order header shows one badge next to the status: "Internal" for an internal work order, "No Charge" for a no-charge work order (a different style from Internal), in the desktop and the mobile header. It is the only mark on the work order: the customer card on the detail page shows no badge and no category. On the detail page the header card of an internal or no-charge work order has an orange outline and a light orange background (a new style for the header card, on desktop and on the mobile header; the design authority names the token), so the work order is recognised at a glance; there is no hint sentence under the header. The category of a no-charge work order is not shown on the work order; it is in the Change category dialog, on the NO CHARGE document and in the report (S2-R16). A billable work order that carries no-charge lines carries no badge and no header style; the line carries the mark (Story 12).”
  • Feature Overview: “Both look and work like a normal work order until the end. Estimates, approvals, parts ordering, picking, receiving, clocking and the review step work exactly as today. Lines show quantity, cost and hours and no sell prices: no labor rate, no part price, no totals, no tax, no fees, no discounts. Shop supplies is one flat amount (below). Nobody zeroes anything. One badge, "Internal" or "No Charge", shows next to the status wherever the work order appears, and on the detail page the header card is outlined in orange so nobody invoices it by habit.”

Change category opens the dialog "Change category for work order [number]" with the Category select (the current category preselected) and, when the new category requires it, the Original work order and Original line selects of S2-R2 (changing to a category that does not require them clears them) and the buttons Cancel and Save; Save is enabled once the category, the original work order or the original line differs from the current values (as on a line, S12-R5), so a missing original can be added before Close; it changes nothing else. It is offered while the setting is off too (S2-N1). After Close the category is locked with the classification (S2-R9); a wrong category on a closed work order is fixed by Reopen, Change category and Close again, an accepted cost of one lock for everything. Cancelling or dismissing any of these leaves the work order as it was. From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.0 final (9 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11759 (Story 2, An internal or no-charge work order from creation to Close), story SV-11760 (Story 3, Close an internal or no-charge work order)

fields.title: An internal job goes from creation to Closed without editing a price
fields.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Make sure the Internal Work Orders setting is on in Settings > Work Orders.
  • Make sure the test location has no accounting integration (neither QuickBooks Online nor AccountingHub).
  • Make sure Require Review Before Completion is off in Settings > Work Orders.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer A, flagged as an Internal customer, with one asset, asset 1.
fields.custom_steps:
1. Click New Work Order.
  2. Pick customer A.
  3. Pick asset 1.
  4. Click Save in the New Work Order window.
  5. Add a labor line of 1.5 hours.
  6. Complete the line.
  7. Click Close Work Order in the work order header.
  8. Click Close Work Order in the confirmation.
fields.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The New Work Order window opens.

Step 2:

  • The "Internal" badge shows.

Step 3:

  • Asset 1 is picked.

Step 4:

  • The work order opens with the "Internal" badge.

Step 5:

  • The line shows 1.5 hours and no price field was asked for.

Step 6:

  • The line is Complete.

Step 7:

  • The Close confirmation opens.

Step 8:

  • The work order shows the status Closed with the "Internal" badge; no sell price was ever entered.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.0 final (9 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11759 (Story 2, An internal or no-charge work order from creation to Close), story SV-11760 (Story 3, Close an internal or no-charge work order)

  • Goals: “An advisor can take an internal or no-charge job from creation to Closed without editing a single sell price.”
  • Feature Overview: “Both close the same way. Where a billable work order shows Create invoice, these show Close Work Order. One confirmation shows the posting date, the parts cost and the account it posts to, special-order parts and sublet, the shop supplies amount, and the labor hours on the lines, which are not posted. Confirming closes the work order: Closed · Internal or Closed · No Charge. Nothing is owed, nothing goes to receivables, no payment is recorded, no email, portal notification or invoice webhook is sent (the work order status webhook of Story 11 is), no tax or fees are added. The closed work order keeps a downloadable document stamped NO CHARGE, with parts at cost, labor in hours and, on a no-charge work order, the category, as proof of repair for a warranty claim or an auditor. Reopen Work Order reverses exactly what was posted and returns the work order to Complete.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.

fields.title: A failed conversion shows an alert and keeps the classification
fields.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Make sure the Internal Work Orders setting is on in Settings > Work Orders.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer A.
  • Have a new work order for this test, work order 1, for customer A, Approved.
fields.custom_steps:
1. Open work order 1.
  2. Open the work order's three-dots menu.
  3. Click "Convert to No Charge".
  4. Pick "Goodwill" in Category.
  5. Click the confirming Convert to No Charge button.
fields.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Work order 1 opens.

Step 2:

  • The menu shows "Convert to No Charge".

Step 3:

  • The confirmation opens.

Step 4:

  • Goodwill is picked.

Step 5:

  • When the change fails, an alert toast that must be dismissed reads "Could not change the work order. Try again."
  • The work order stays billable.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.0 final (9 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11758 (Story 1, Turn on Internal Work Orders, flag internal customers, manage categories), story SV-11759 (Story 2, An internal or no-charge work order from creation to Close)

  • Story 2, Error Handling: “If converting, or changing the category, fails, display "Could not change the work order. Try again." as an alert toast that must be dismissed; the work order keeps its previous classification.”
  • User Feedback Summary: “Save, change, close or reopen fails | "Could not save the internal customer. Try again." / "Could not change the work order. Try again." / "Could not close the work order. Try again." / "Could not reopen the work order. Try again." | Alert toast, must be dismissed”
